newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-Baabaas romp in Huddersfield snow.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Baabaas romp in Huddersfield snow.

text.p: HUDDERSFIELD, Nov 24 - The touring New Zealand Barbarians overwhelmed a scratch Northern Counties team 86-0, scoring 14 tries on a snow-bound McAlpine Stadium, NZPA reported on Monday (NZT).
Ignoring the cold and wet and the slippery underfoot conditions, the Barbarians provided superb entertainment for the 5000 hardy spectators who turned up on a bitterly cold day.
Preparation it may have been for the Barbarians' international against England next week, but it could hardly be described as a warm-up.

Temperatures touched freezing and snow fell before and for the first hour of the game, giving the game a surreal atmosphere more associated with Christmas card scenes than international rugby matches.
It was so cold that in the closing minutes the Barbarians elected not to take conversions of their increasing number of tries in an effort to speed up the game.
The Barbarians were also faced with a side made up mainly of English second and third division players after most of the North's original team withdrew on Friday.
They replacements did their best, but could not cope with the pace, strength and teamwork of the tourists.
The first try came after five minutes, through No.8 Taine Randell, and after leading 40-0 at half time the Barbarians piled on 32 points in the closing quarter as the North's brave resistance faded.
First five-eighth Carlos Spencer kicked seven conversions and scored a try for a personal tally of 19 points, before replacement Andrew Mehrtens took over the kicking duties.
Wing Joeli Vidiri scored a second-half hat trick, and openside flanker Andrew Blowers also scored three tries as well as featuring strongly around the field.

If Blowers was the pick of the Barbarians, it was not by much. Spencer had an excellent game at first five-eighth before moving to fullback to make way for Mehrtens, Jonah Lomu made some telling bursts which led to tries, although he did not get on the scoresheet himself.

In fact, while Lomu often found himself contained by two or three defenders, when the ball was recycled at the breakdown there were often gaps on the right. Vidiri's hat trick, and right wing tries for Cullen and Spencer bore testimony to Lomu's contribution.
Prop Mark Allen had a busy game while Cullen also looked in good form before going off after 46 minutes.
Coach John Hart complimented his players for their application throughout 80 difficult minutes in conditions alien to all of them.
"I don't think many of our players had played in snow before. In fact I think one or two of them may not have even seen snow before," Hart said.
"It was a terrific performance really. I was thrilled with the way the boys played.
"There were some great skills on show there and to keep up our skill and intensity levels for the whole match was a great effort."
The Barbarians held the upper hand from early in the match, and scored their early tries from close range.

Cullen threw an outrageous dummy 25m out to score his first try and make it 31-0, then from a North scrum halfback Justin Marshall cheekily stole the ball from under the nose of his opposite David Scully, and passed for Blowers to score his second try at the end of the first half.
Vidiri came on as a half time replacement for Glen Osborne, and had his first try after 17 minutes of the second half.
Oozing confidence, he strode in for his second try, teasing the defence to tackle him.
His third try started from a chip over the defence by Lee Stensness some 60 metres out, which was gathered in by Mehrtens who then put Vidiri clear.
As the Barbarians galloped away with the game in the closing minutes, replacement halfback Mark Robinson showed outstanding pace to kick ahead and score in the left wing corner.
The tourists used 19 players in a liberal interpretation of the new replacement rule, including lock Ian Jones who only arrived from Fiji at 5.30am.
Teams:

New Zealand Barbarians: Christian Cullen (Andrew Mehrtens 46), Glen Osborne (Joeli Vidiri half time), Alama Ieremia (Mark Ranby 66), Jonah Lomu, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Justin Marshall (Mark Robinson 71), Taine Randell, Andrew Blowers, Robin Brooke, Glenn Taylor (Ian Jones 60), Dylan Mika, Olo Brown, Sean Fitzpatrick (c) Mark Allen.

Northern Counties: Peter Massey, Richard Thompson, John Harper (Steve Burnhill 62), Greg Anderton (Steve Cooke 69), David Lyon, Simon Binns, David Scully, John Dudley, Peter Anglesea, Paul Stewart (Andrew Luddiman 58), Paul Rees, Paul Manley, Stuart Turner, Terry Garnet, Michael Worsley (Rod Latham
